title: Advances in Individual Detector Characterization and Key Parameters that Affect Modern EDS Performance
content: Since the availability of FE-SEMs in the late ‘90s, large area SDD detectors in the late 2010’s [1] and high solid angle windowless detectors from the mid 2015’s [2], imaging and elemental characterisation of nano-structures in the SEM has become a reality. These systems allow low landing energies and small beam diameter, resulting in smaller interaction volume and improved spatial resolution, while being able to collect sufficient electrons and X-rays for structural and chemical characterisation of samples. Low energy X-ray nano-analysis comes with many challenges, including the complexities of X-ray generation, absorption and emission which do not affect conventional microanalysis at higher X-ray energies. There are also significant instrumental challenges to designing EDS detectors and spectrum processing algorithms that can accurately detect and separate the low energy X-ray signals emitted from the sample when using low beam landing energies. In this study we consider recent hardware and spectrum processing developments to improve spectral resolution and model the incomplete charge collection of individual detectors, and their benefits on solving characterisation challenges of nano-structures.
